title: Remove Setting Method

solutions.title: A private field the constructor is the only writer of
solutions.tradeoff: A mis-numbered ticket can no longer be corrected in place - fixing a bad serial now means voiding the ticket and issuing a new one instead of patching the one you have, and this drill does not build the voiding workflow that would make that a fair trade.

reviewFocus: Does `Ticket` still expose any way to change `id` after construction - a `setId`, a public field, a second constructor - or is the private field truly the only place it is ever assigned?
Is `holderName` still settable through `transferTo`, and does the walkthrough say why that setter earns its place when `setId` didn't?
Does `tests-fixed/` prove only the one thing that changed - that a freshly issued ticket is findable by its own id - without depending on anything `tests/` already pins?
Does the walkthrough show why plain `readonly` cannot coexist with the old `setId` in the same class, rather than asserting it?
Does the walkthrough name a concrete case where `readonly` would not have been enough, or does it reach for `#private` everywhere out of caution?
